bibliographic.title: Productivity of incident management with conversational bots-a review
bibliographic.authors: Orlando Iparraguirre-Villanueva; Luz Obregon-Palomino; Wilson Pujay-Iglesias; Fernando Sierra-Liñan; Michael Cabanillas-Carbonell
bibliographic.venue: IAES International Journal of Artificial Intelligence (IJ-AI)
bibliographic.citation_apa: Iparraguirre-Villanueva, O., Obregon-Palomino, L., Pujay-Iglesias, W., Sierra-Liñan, F., & Cabanillas-Carbonell, M. (2023). Productivity of incident management with conversational bots-a review. IAES International Journal of Artificial Intelligence, 12(4), 1543-1556. https://doi.org/10.11591/ijai.v12.i4.pp1543-1556

methodology.sample_description: Articles from 2019 to 2022 retrieved from Scopus, Springer, Wiley, Indexes-Csic, Taylor & Francis, Pubmed, and Ebsco Host; 47 relevant articles systematized
methodology.sector: incident management; information systems; customer service; healthcare; education; IT
methodology.technology_context: conversational agents, chatbots, AI, NLP, conversational interfaces, virtual assistants

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article is a peer-reviewed systematic review on conversational bots in incident management with PRISMA and coverage of healthcare and education, which aligns partially with conversational AI in high-stakes contexts. However, the provided text does not mention large language models, governance, compliance, audit, guardrails, human oversight, accountability, or post-deployment monitoring as study objectives or findings. Relevance to conversational governance in LLM-based regulated systems is therefore indirect and weak.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Borderline fit: strong conversational-bot and SLR signals, but no explicit LLM or governance content in supplied excerpts; full text needed to confirm absence of governance themes and LLM-related technologies.

appraisal.notes: Clear SLR objective and PRISMA reporting with named databases and 47 included articles. Analysis includes taxonomy tables and network mapping. Ethics, limitations, and governance dimensions are not evidenced in the supplied text.

cerqual.explanation: Methodological reporting is moderately strong for a systematic review, with coherent focus on productivity, bot types, and processes. Adequacy is moderate because governance and LLM-specific concerns are not addressed. Relevance to the review's governance-in-regulated-LLM scope is low based on available text.

coding.theme: Productivity and application of conversational bots in incident management
coding.subtheme: Systematic synthesis of bot types, benefits, and optimized processes

synthesis.main_claim: Conversational agents in company-managed information systems increase productivity in incident management and related processes; a systematic review of 47 articles (2019-2022) identifies key benefits, nine bot types, prominent optimized processes, and proposes an architecture model for conversational bots in incident management.
synthesis.contribution: Provides a PRISMA-based synthesis of conversational bot literature focused on productivity, classifies bot types and application processes across domains including healthcare and education, and proposes an architecture model for incident management.
synthesis.use_in_review: Potential supporting or contextual evidence for conversational AI in operational and partially regulated domains, but not central evidence for LLM-based conversational governance because governance, oversight, compliance, and LLM-specific technologies are not evidenced in the supplied text.
